name: Getting started with GGMoney
description: Set up payments and understand your statements.

cards.subject: The bank feed
says: brings bank transactions into GGMoney through Open Banking
is the day-to-day route for getting transactions in without uploading files
has to be pointed at one of your bank accounts before anything syncs
cards.use: want transactions to arrive without uploading statement files
not: lets GGMoney make payments out of your bank account

cards.subject: Bank CSV import
says: loads transactions from a statement file you upload
covers banks no provider supports, closed accounts and older history
writes to the same place as the bank feed
cards.use: need to load the history of a closed account
not: is the only way to get any transaction into GGMoney

cards.subject: The compliance calendar
says: lists tax and filing duties as records with due dates
drives the deadline reminder emails
states that its dates are reminders, not advice
cards.use: want to see which filing deadlines are coming up
not: gives personal tax advice for your situation

cards.subject: A posted journal
says: is never edited or deleted once it has been posted
is corrected by posting a reversal
leaves both the mistake and the fix visible in the books
cards.use: need to fix a wrong entry that has already been posted
not: can be quietly overwritten by the owner

cards.subject: A person's role in a company
says: is one of owner, accountant or viewer
is held separately for each company the person belongs to
cards.use: want to know how access to a company's books is labelled
not: is the same for every company a person belongs to

cards.subject: Company and individual records
says: are kept as separate entity types
mean a company's books and a person's tax profile are not the same kind of record
cards.use: wonder why a personal profile is not treated like a company
not: are stored as one combined record type

cards.subject: Whole pence
says: are how GGMoney stores every money value, as an integer
avoid the rounding drift that decimal fractions can introduce
cards.use: want to know how GGMoney avoids fractions of a penny creeping into totals
not: are replaced by floating-point numbers when totals are large

cards.subject: Basis points
says: hold a percentage as an integer, so 20 percent is stored as 2000
keep rates exact in the same way whole pence keep amounts exact
cards.use: see a rate stored as a large whole number rather than a percentage
not: are hundredths of a basis, so 20 percent is 20

cards.subject: Sandbox mode
says: runs against provider and HMRC test services rather than live ones
is used to practise before real credentials and approval exist
means nothing is really filed with HMRC
cards.use: want to try a filing without it being real
not: files real returns but marks them as drafts

cards.subject: The payslip
says: shows pay and deductions for one pay period
is given to the employee
shows its workings in full in GGMoney
cards.use: want to see how a figure on a payslip was reached
not: is optional and has no link to payroll figures

cards.subject: The trial balance
says: lists every account's balance so that debits equal credits
is one of the reports GGMoney produces from the ledger
is a check on the books before the other statements are drawn up
cards.use: want a quick check that the books balance
not: shows only profit for the year

cards.subject: The Open Banking providers behind GGMoney
says: include GoCardless, TrueLayer and Plaid
sit behind one common bank connector
cards.use: ask which providers sit behind GGMoney's bank connections
not: come from a single built-in bank only

cards.subject: Invoices and bills in GGMoney
says: cover sales invoices you issue and purchase bills you receive
link to the contacts they were raised for
cards.use: want to record who owes you and whom you owe
not: are only recorded through bank statement import

cards.subject: Email from GGMoney
says: carries payslips, invoices and deadline alerts
is guarded so nothing sends when no email key is configured
cards.use: wonder why no email arrives from a test setup
not: is always sent even in a test setup

cards.subject: Open Banking
says: lets you share your bank data with an approved provider with your consent
does not require you to hand your banking password to the provider
is the regulated route that bank feeds in finance software use
cards.use: want a regulated way to share bank data with software
not: lets any website move money out of your account without asking

cards.subject: Read-only access
says: lets software see transactions but not move money
is the scope GGMoney asks bank-data providers for
limits the harm if a connection is ever misused
cards.use: want to be sure a connected tool cannot pay anyone
not: lets software approve payments up to a daily limit

cards.subject: Your online banking password
says: is never seen by GGMoney
is typed only on your bank's own login screen
should never be given to a tool, a helper or a caller
cards.use: are asked by a message to send your banking password
not: is passed to GGMoney once and then stored

cards.subject: Bank consent
says: is the permission you give for a provider to read your bank data
expires and has to be renewed
can be withdrawn by you
cards.use: need to understand why a feed stops after a while
not: lasts forever once you approve it

cards.subject: Consent length under UK Open Banking
says: is at most 90 days
means a feed will need your approval again after that time
cards.use: ask how long a UK Open Banking connection lasts before renewal
not: is one year for every provider

cards.subject: The renewal warning
says: appears from 14 days before consent ends
gives you time to renew before the feed stops
cards.use: want to avoid a gap in your transactions
not: appears only after the feed has stopped

cards.subject: Pointing a feed at an account
says: links a connected feed to one of your bank accounts in GGMoney
is needed before anything syncs
cannot be done twice for the same account by two feeds
cards.use: have connected a bank but no transactions appear
not: happens automatically the moment you approve the bank

cards.subject: The first sync
says: takes everything the bank allows
brings in the longest history the connection provides
cards.use: connect a feed for the first time
not: reads only the last week of transactions

cards.subject: Later syncs
says: re-read the last week of transactions
pick up items that posted late
cards.use: wonder how a late-posting payment reaches the books
not: repeat the whole history each time

cards.subject: The account opening date
says: causes earlier transactions to be skipped
marks where an account's records begin
cards.use: see old transactions that were not imported
not: stops all transactions after it from importing

cards.subject: Duplicate recognition across routes
says: treats a transaction that arrives by both feed and CSV as one
protects totals when two routes overlap
cards.use: import a statement file for a period the feed already covers
not: doubles the transaction so that you can delete one copy

cards.subject: Bank reconciliation
says: compares your records with the bank statement
finds items that appear on one side only
is how you prove your books agree with the bank
cards.use: want to confirm your records match the bank
not: is the process of paying all bills at once

cards.subject: A bank statement
says: is the bank's own record of money in and out of an account
is the evidence your books are checked against
cards.use: need independent evidence of what the bank holds
not: is created by your own bookkeeping records

cards.subject: A reconciled transaction
says: has been matched to a statement line
is left unchanged by later syncs because it may sit in a filed VAT return
cards.use: wonder why a sync did not alter a matched line
not: is edited freely by every sync

cards.subject: An unreconciled item
says: has no match yet between the books and the bank
needs investigating or matching
cards.use: see a line that is in the bank but not your books
not: has already been confirmed against the statement

cards.subject: The opening balance
says: is the starting figure when you begin recording an account
should agree to the statement at that date
cards.use: start recording an account that already holds money
not: is calculated from the next month's sales

cards.subject: The closing balance
says: is the balance at the end of a statement period
should equal the next period's opening balance
cards.use: check that one statement period joins the next
not: is the balance at the start of the period

cards.subject: A timing difference
says: arises when a payment is recorded but has not yet cleared
usually clears itself within a few days
cards.use: see a recorded cheque missing from the statement
not: is a sign of fraud every time

cards.subject: A bank charge missing from the books
says: appears on the statement but not in your records
needs recording as an expense
cards.use: find a fee on the statement that you never entered
not: is a mistake the bank must reverse

cards.subject: Automatic transaction matching
says: merges two transactions only when account, date and amount match
does not merge when more than one candidate fits
cards.use: worry that two similar payments could be wrongly merged
not: merges any two transactions with the same amount

cards.subject: An unexplained transaction
says: has no known purpose
should be queried before it is categorised
can be an early sign of fraud or error
cards.use: find a payment nobody recognises
not: is safest to categorise as miscellaneous and move on

cards.subject: Regular reconciliation
says: catches errors and fraud early
is easier monthly than once a year
cards.use: want problems found while they are still easy to trace
not: is only needed at year end

cards.subject: A sales invoice
says: bills a customer for goods or services you supplied
creates money owed to you
cards.use: need to ask a customer to pay
not: records something you bought from a supplier

cards.subject: A purchase bill
says: records what you owe a supplier
creates a payable until you pay it
cards.use: receive an invoice from a supplier
not: is issued to your customer

cards.subject: A contact
says: stores the details of a customer or supplier
is attached to the invoices and bills raised for it
cards.use: need one place for a customer's or supplier's details
not: holds the company's own bank statement

cards.subject: A credit note
says: reduces or cancels an invoice already issued
is the proper way to correct an invoice instead of deleting it
cards.use: need to correct an issued invoice without erasing it
not: is a new invoice for an extra amount

cards.subject: Payment terms
says: set how many days a customer has to pay
are shown on the invoice
cards.use: agree how long a customer may take to pay
not: are the fees charged for paying early

cards.subject: The invoice number sequence
says: gives each invoice a unique, ordered reference
makes a missing document easy to spot
cards.use: want to see at a glance whether an invoice is missing
not: can be reused after an invoice is cancelled

cards.subject: A purchase order
says: authorises a purchase before the supplier invoices
lets the bill be checked against what was approved
cards.use: want to approve spending before it happens
not: is sent to a customer to request payment

cards.subject: A receipt
says: is evidence that a payment was made
supports the expense claimed in the books
cards.use: need proof that something was paid for
not: is the same as an unpaid invoice

cards.subject: A payment allocation
says: matches a payment against the invoices or bills it settles
lets one payment cover several invoices
lets a part payment leave a balance still due
cards.use: receive one payment that covers two invoices
not: can only match one invoice per payment

cards.subject: An overdue invoice
says: remains unpaid after its due date
calls for a polite reminder first
cards.use: find an invoice past its due date
not: is automatically cancelled after the due date

cards.subject: A supplier statement
says: lists what the supplier believes you owe
is compared with your bills to find missing ones
cards.use: want to find a bill you have not recorded
not: replaces the need to record bills

cards.subject: VAT
says: is a tax added to most goods and services in the UK
is collected by registered businesses and passed to HMRC
cards.use: ask what the tax on an invoice is for
not: is a tax on a business's profit only

cards.subject: Output VAT
says: is the VAT you charge on your sales
is owed to HMRC
cards.use: want the VAT you have charged customers
not: is the VAT you pay on purchases

cards.subject: Input VAT
says: is the VAT you pay on purchases
can usually be reclaimed by a registered business
cards.use: want the VAT you have paid suppliers
not: is the VAT you charge customers

cards.subject: A VAT return
says: summarises VAT due on sales and reclaimable on purchases for a period
is sent to HMRC at set intervals
cards.use: need to report VAT for a period
not: is filed once a year with the accounts

cards.subject: The standard VAT accounting scheme
says: bases VAT on the dates of invoices
puts a sale in the return even if the customer has not paid yet
cards.use: want VAT counted when the invoice is issued
not: bases VAT on when cash is received

cards.subject: The cash accounting scheme
says: bases VAT on when money is paid or received
suits businesses whose customers pay late
cards.use: have customers who pay slowly and want to pay VAT only after they do
not: bases VAT on the invoice date

cards.subject: The flat rate scheme
says: applies a set percentage to turnover to work out the payment
simplifies calculating VAT
cards.use: want to pay VAT as a fixed percentage rather than tracking each purchase
not: bases every figure on actual invoice dates and input VAT

cards.subject: Making Tax Digital for VAT
says: requires digital records and submission through software
sends VAT returns to HMRC from compatible software
cards.use: ask why a VAT return is sent from software
not: lets you post paper returns instead

cards.subject: Finalising a VAT return
says: freezes the figures before sending
is a different step from submitting
cards.use: want the figures locked for review before filing
not: sends the return to HMRC

cards.subject: Submitting a VAT return
says: needs its own declaration
cannot be withdrawn because HMRC has no way to withdraw a return
cards.use: are ready to send a finalised return
not: can be undone by deleting the draft

cards.subject: The reverse charge
says: makes the customer account for VAT on certain supplies
moves the VAT accounting from supplier to customer
cards.use: buy a service where the customer must account for the VAT
not: adds a second charge on top of normal VAT

cards.subject: Rounding in VAT boxes 6 to 9
says: goes down to whole pounds
is different from the penny rounding used in payroll
cards.use: wonder why pence disappear from some VAT boxes
not: rounds to the nearest penny

cards.subject: Gross pay
says: is pay before any deductions
is the starting point on a payslip
cards.use: want to see pay before tax
not: is take-home pay

cards.subject: Net pay
says: is take-home pay after deductions
is what reaches the employee's bank account
cards.use: want to know what the employee receives
not: is pay before tax

cards.subject: PAYE
says: collects income tax from wages through the employer
is paid over to HMRC by the employer
cards.use: ask how income tax on wages reaches HMRC
not: is the tax charged on a company's profit

cards.subject: National Insurance
says: is a separate contribution from income tax
is deducted from pay and also paid by the employer
cards.use: see a deduction that is not income tax
not: is the same deduction as income tax

cards.subject: A tax code
says: tells the employer how much tax-free pay to allow
affects how much PAYE is taken
cards.use: find that the tax taken seems wrong
not: is chosen by the employee each month

cards.subject: A student loan deduction
says: is taken from pay above a threshold
is calculated by the payroll software
cards.use: see a deduction for a student loan
not: is paid directly by the employer from company funds

cards.subject: A workplace pension
says: has contributions from the employee and the employer
is shown as a deduction on the payslip
cards.use: see a pension amount on a payslip
not: is paid only by the employer

cards.subject: Statutory pay
says: is pay required by law, such as sick or maternity pay
has its own rules in the payroll calculation
cards.use: need to pay an employee who is off sick or on leave
not: is optional bonus pay

cards.subject: Real Time Information
says: reports pay and deductions to HMRC each time staff are paid
cards.use: ask how HMRC learns about each pay run
not: is a once-a-year report

cards.subject: Rounding in payroll
says: differs by tax on purpose
rounds PAYE down to the penny
rounds student loan figures down to whole pounds
cards.use: wonder why different deductions round differently
not: uses one rounding rule for every figure

cards.subject: The verified tax year rule
says: stops payroll being filed for a year whose rates are not verified
protects against filing with wrong rates
cards.use: see that payroll will not file for a new tax year yet
not: lets payroll be filed with last year's rates

cards.subject: The profit and loss account
says: shows income less costs over a period
tells you whether the business made a profit
cards.use: want to see whether the business made money over a period
not: lists what the business owns and owes on one date

cards.subject: The balance sheet
says: shows what the business owns and owes on one date
has assets on one side and liabilities and equity on the other
cards.use: want a snapshot of the business on one date
not: shows income and costs over a year

cards.subject: A cash flow statement
says: shows money moving in and out over a period
can show profit while cash is short
cards.use: want to see why cash is short despite profit
not: lists what customers owe

cards.subject: An aged debtors report
says: groups unpaid customer invoices by how overdue they are
helps decide whom to chase first
cards.use: want to see which customer invoices are most overdue
not: groups money owed to suppliers

cards.subject: An aged creditors report
says: groups unpaid supplier bills by age
helps plan which suppliers to pay
cards.use: want to see which supplier bills are most overdue
not: groups money owed by customers

cards.subject: A chart of accounts
says: lists the categories used to record income, costs, assets and liabilities
gives each category a name and code
cards.use: want to see how transactions are categorised
not: lists customers and suppliers

cards.subject: Double-entry bookkeeping
says: records every transaction as a debit and a credit
keeps debits and credits equal
cards.use: ask why every entry has two sides
not: records each transaction once

cards.subject: The general ledger
says: holds all of a company's accounts
is where journals post
cards.use: need the full record behind the reports
not: lists only the customers

cards.subject: Year-end accounts
says: summarise a company's results for its financial year
are built from the ledger
cards.use: ask what a company produces at the end of its financial year
not: are produced weekly

cards.subject: Phishing
says: tricks you into revealing details by email
often copies a trusted brand
tries to get you to click a link or open an attachment
cards.use: receive an email asking you to sign in via a link
not: is a technical attack that needs no action from you

cards.subject: Smishing
says: is phishing by text message
often claims a delivery or a bank problem
cards.use: get a text asking you to confirm details via a link
not: is phishing by phone call

cards.subject: Vishing
says: is phishing by phone call
often pretends to be a bank or HMRC
cards.use: get a call urging you to move money to a safe account
not: is phishing by text message

cards.subject: Social engineering
says: manipulates people rather than technology
relies on urgency, authority or fear
cards.use: ask why scammers target people rather than systems
not: breaks encryption directly

cards.subject: A fake HMRC message
says: threatens penalties or promises a refund
asks for personal or payment details
pressures you to act at once
cards.use: get a message claiming you owe tax and must pay now
not: is always sent from a verified HMRC address

cards.subject: Mandate fraud
says: asks you to change a supplier's bank details
usually arrives as a request that looks like it came from the supplier
cards.use: receive a request to change a supplier's bank details
not: is a bank error in a standing order

cards.subject: Chief executive fraud
says: impersonates a senior person to demand an urgent payment
relies on staff reluctance to question authority
cards.use: get an urgent message that appears to be from the boss asking for payment
not: is a request from a supplier to change bank details

cards.subject: Account takeover
says: uses stolen login details to act as you
is far harder with a second sign-in step
cards.use: find activity you did not do on an account
not: only happens when a device is stolen

cards.subject: A fake invoice
says: bills for goods or services never ordered
hopes the bill is paid without checking
cards.use: receive an invoice for something nobody recalls ordering
not: is a genuine bill with a late fee

cards.subject: An overpayment scam
says: sends too much money and asks for the difference back
relies on the original payment later being reversed
cards.use: are paid too much and asked to refund the difference
not: is a bank mistake that is safe to refund at once

cards.subject: Authorised push payment fraud
says: tricks you into sending the money yourself
is hard to reverse once the payment has gone
cards.use: are talked into making a payment yourself by a caller
not: is the same as an unauthorised card payment

cards.subject: Business email compromise
says: takes over a real email account to redirect payments
makes a fraudulent request look genuine
cards.use: suspect a real colleague's email account is being misused
not: is a spam email sent to many people

cards.subject: A strong, unique password
says: is long and different for every account
limits the damage if one account leaks
cards.use: set a password for a new account
not: can safely be reused if it is long

cards.subject: A password manager
says: stores and fills unique passwords
can warn you when a site address looks wrong
cards.use: cannot remember many different passwords
not: stores your passwords in one note on your phone

cards.subject: A second sign-in step
says: asks for something more than your password
blocks most attacks that use only a stolen password
cards.use: want to protect an account even if the password leaks
not: replaces the need for a password

cards.subject: Signing out of a shared device
says: ends your session so the next user cannot use it
is important after using a borrowed device
cards.use: finish using a computer someone else can access
not: is unnecessary if you close the window

cards.subject: Locking your screen
says: stops others using your session while you are away
should be done whenever you step away
cards.use: leave your desk for a few minutes
not: is only needed overnight

cards.subject: Checking the web address
says: helps confirm you are on the real site
looks for the exact domain before you sign in
cards.use: are about to sign in from a link in an email
not: is satisfied by a padlock alone

cards.subject: Not clicking unexpected links
says: avoids landing on a fake sign-in page
means going to the site yourself instead
cards.use: get a message that urges you to click a link
not: is safe when the message uses a known logo

cards.subject: Keeping software updated
says: closes known security holes
applies to devices, browsers and apps
cards.use: see an update notification for your browser
not: only matters for new features

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person only the access they need
limits what a mistake or a stolen account can do
cards.use: decide how much access to give a new helper
not: gives everyone full access to avoid delays

cards.subject: Reviewing access when someone leaves
says: removes their access promptly
closes a common gap in small businesses
cards.use: need to handle a team member leaving the business
not: can wait until the next audit

cards.subject: Calling back on a known number
says: checks an unexpected request using contact details you already trust
avoids using numbers supplied in the message
cards.use: get a call asking you to confirm payment details
not: uses the number the caller gives you

cards.subject: Public Wi-Fi
says: is a risk for sensitive work
is safer to avoid for banking and finance tools
cards.use: need to check your bank in a cafe
not: is as safe as your home network

cards.subject: Recovery codes
says: let you regain access if you lose your second step
should be stored safely and offline
cards.use: set up a second sign-in step
not: are shared with support to unlock your account

cards.subject: The four-eyes principle
says: requires a second person to check important actions
reduces both mistakes and fraud
cards.use: want a second pair of eyes on a payment
not: lets one person approve their own work

cards.subject: Second-person approval of filings
says: is required in GGMoney for filings
is refused by the app if the same person tries to approve their own filing
cards.use: ask who must approve a filing in GGMoney
not: is optional for filings and required for routine tasks

cards.subject: Routine task approval
says: needs only one person in GGMoney
is lighter than the check needed for a filing
cards.use: ask how many people must approve a routine compliance task
not: needs two people for every task

cards.subject: Segregation of duties
says: splits the tasks of requesting, approving and paying
stops one person controlling a whole transaction
cards.use: design who may raise and who may pay a bill
not: gives one person every step for speed

cards.subject: An approval limit
says: caps what one person can approve alone
sends larger amounts to someone senior
cards.use: set how much one person may approve
not: is set to unlimited for owners

cards.subject: An audit trail
says: records who did what and when
lets you reconstruct how a figure came about
cards.use: need to trace who changed a record
not: is deleted once a period is closed

cards.subject: An irreversible submission
says: cannot be taken back once sent
calls for a check and a declaration first
cards.use: are about to send something that cannot be withdrawn
not: can be recalled from the recipient

cards.subject: An automatic check
says: reports a problem but never signs anything off
leaves the decision to a person
cards.use: see a check that flags an issue on a filing
not: approves the filing automatically if clean

cards.subject: Review before filing
says: catches errors while they can be fixed
is the step between finalising and submitting
cards.use: want to catch mistakes before sending
not: happens after the filing is sent

cards.subject: Delegation
says: passes a task to another person with defined limits
does not remove the delegator's accountability
cards.use: ask someone to approve payments while you are away
not: transfers all responsibility to the delegate

cards.subject: Sign-off
says: is a named person's recorded approval
shows who accepted a piece of work
cards.use: need a record that a task was accepted
not: is an automatic status that needs no person

cards.subject: Keeping receipts
says: keeps the evidence for each expense
should be done as the spending happens
cards.use: just paid for something for the business
not: can wait until the year end

cards.subject: A separate business bank account
says: keeps business money apart from personal money
makes reconciliation and reporting simpler
cards.use: want to avoid mixing personal and business spending
not: is unnecessary for a company

cards.subject: Digital records
says: are searchable and easy to back up
are required for VAT under Making Tax Digital
cards.use: ask why paper records alone are not enough for VAT
not: replace the need for any backup

cards.subject: Backups
says: protect against loss of records
are best kept off the machine they copy
cards.use: worry about losing your books
not: are enough if kept on the same device

cards.subject: A monthly close
says: finishes the month's records before the next begins
reconciles bank accounts and reviews unusual items
cards.use: want a regular routine for finishing the books
not: is done only at the financial year end

cards.subject: A mileage log
says: records journeys for business travel claims
includes date, purpose and distance
cards.use: drive for business and plan to claim
not: is needed only for company cars

cards.subject: Evidence for every entry
says: means each figure can be traced to a document
supports an answer to any query about the books
cards.use: are asked to justify an entry in the books
not: lets you record entries without a document

cards.subject: Record retention
says: means keeping records for the period the law requires
applies to business and tax records
cards.use: wonder when old records can be discarded
not: lets records be discarded at the end of each month

cards.subject: Describing a problem precisely
says: says what you did, what you expected and what happened
helps support solve the problem faster
cards.use: need to report a problem
not: is just 'it does not work'

cards.subject: Sharing a screenshot safely
says: hides passwords, codes and account numbers
gives support the evidence without exposing secrets
cards.use: want to send a screenshot to support
not: includes the full page with every detail

cards.subject: Never sharing your password with support
says: is a rule for any genuine support team
protects you from impersonators
cards.use: are asked by 'support' for your password
not: is safe once the caller proves their name

cards.subject: Checking that support is genuine
says: uses contact details you found yourself
avoids replying to unsolicited offers of help
cards.use: get an unexpected message offering help with your account
not: trusts the contact in the message

cards.subject: Asking an accountant
says: suits tax decisions and unusual transactions
goes beyond what a reminder calendar can say
cards.use: face a tax decision for your situation
not: is replaced by calendar reminders

cards.subject: Reporting suspected fraud
says: starts with telling your bank at once
includes reporting to the national fraud service
cards.use: think you have sent money to a scammer
not: can wait until you are sure

cards.subject: A support reference number
says: identifies your case
lets you follow up without repeating everything
cards.use: need to follow up on a support request
not: is used as a password

cards.subject: Escalating a problem
says: raises it to someone senior when the first reply fails
includes the earlier reference and what was tried
cards.use: have not got an answer after repeated attempts
not: means starting a fresh unrelated request

cards.subject: Calendar dates are reminders, not advice
says: is what the compliance calendar says about its dates
means you must confirm the date on the official source
cards.use: rely on a calendar date for a filing
not: means the date is legally binding in the app

cards.subject: Cash flow
says: is the movement of money in and out of a business
can be tight even when a business is profitable
cards.use: ask whether the business can pay bills next month
not: is the same as annual profit

cards.subject: Profit
says: is income less costs for a period
can exist before the money has arrived
cards.use: compare earnings with the bank balance
not: is the amount in the bank

cards.subject: Working capital
says: is current assets less current liabilities
shows whether short-term bills can be met
cards.use: want to know if short-term obligations can be met
not: is the business's long-term borrowing

cards.subject: A budget
says: sets planned income and spending
is compared with actuals to find differences
cards.use: plan spending for the coming months
not: records what was spent last year

cards.subject: A Direct Debit
says: lets a company collect amounts you agreed to
is covered by the Direct Debit Guarantee
cards.use: set up a payment where the amount may vary
not: is a fixed amount you send on a schedule

cards.subject: A standing order
says: sends a fixed amount on a schedule you set
is controlled by you, not by the recipient
cards.use: pay the same amount every month
not: lets the recipient change the amount

cards.subject: Faster Payments
says: is the UK service for near-instant bank transfers
is the usual route for everyday online transfers
cards.use: make an everyday transfer to another UK account
not: is the same as the system for large same-day payments

cards.subject: CHAPS
says: is a UK same-day payment system for high-value transfers
is often used for property purchases
cards.use: need a large payment to arrive the same day
not: is a Direct Debit scheme

cards.subject: Confirmation of Payee
says: checks the name matches the account before a payment
may warn of a mismatch
cards.use: are about to pay a new supplier
not: guarantees the payment is safe

cards.subject: A cash buffer
says: is money set aside for slow months
gives time when customers pay late
cards.use: want to survive a late-paying customer
not: is money kept in the till

cards.subject: A chargeback
says: is a card-payment dispute through the card issuer
may recover money for faulty or undelivered goods
cards.use: pay by card for something never delivered
not: applies to every bank transfer

qa.q: What does GGMoney ask bank-data providers for when connecting a bank feed?
qa.right: Read-only access
wrong: Access to move money between accounts
qa.why: GGMoney asks providers for read-only scopes, so nothing can move money.

qa.q: Where should you type your online banking password?
qa.right: Only on your bank's own login screen
wrong: Into any app that asks for it
Into a message to support so they can check
Into a finance tool so it can sync
qa.why: Open Banking connections are approved on the bank's own screen; GGMoney never sees the password.

qa.q: What is a bank reconciliation?
qa.right: Comparing your records with the bank statement
wrong: Paying all bills in one batch
Asking the bank for a loan
qa.why: Reconciliation checks that your books agree with the bank.

qa.q: What does a sales invoice do?
qa.right: Bills a customer for goods or services you supplied
wrong: Records money you owe a supplier
qa.why: A sales invoice creates money owed to you.

qa.q: What is the safest response to an unexpected email asking you to sign in through a link?
qa.right: Go to the site yourself by typing its address or using a saved bookmark
wrong: Click the link and sign in quickly
Reply asking if it is genuine
Forward it to a colleague and sign in anyway
qa.why: Going to the site yourself avoids a fake sign-in page.

qa.q: What does net pay mean on a payslip?
qa.right: Take-home pay after deductions
qa.why: Net pay is gross pay less deductions.

qa.q: Which GGMoney route brings transactions in without uploading files?
qa.right: The bank feed
qa.why: Bank feeds use Open Banking; CSV import uses a file.

qa.q: What should you do after using a shared computer for your finance tools?
qa.right: Sign out so the next user cannot use your session
wrong: Close the window and leave it
Leave it signed in for the next person
Save the password in the browser
qa.why: Signing out ends the session.

qa.q: How long can UK Open Banking consent last at most?
qa.right: 90 days
qa.why: Consent expires and must be renewed; GGMoney warns from 14 days out.

qa.q: From how many days before consent ends does GGMoney start warning you?
qa.right: 14 days
qa.why: The warning gives time to renew before the feed stops.

qa.q: A bank feed is connected in GGMoney but no transactions appear. What is the most likely missing step?
qa.right: Pointing the feed at one of your bank accounts
wrong: Waiting for the next tax year
qa.why: Nothing syncs until the feed is pointed at an account.

qa.q: What does a compliance calendar date mean in GGMoney?
qa.right: A reminder, not advice
wrong: A legally binding date set by the app
A date the app files for you automatically
qa.why: The generated calendar states that dates are reminders, not advice.

qa.q: Output VAT is...
qa.right: VAT charged on your sales
qa.why: Input VAT is on purchases; output VAT is on sales.

qa.q: Which scheme bases VAT on when money is paid or received?
qa.right: Cash accounting
qa.why: Standard bases VAT on invoice dates; cash accounting on payment dates.

qa.q: What is phishing?
qa.right: Tricking you into revealing details, often by email
wrong: A virus that needs no action from you
qa.why: Phishing relies on you being persuaded to act.

qa.q: Why keep business and personal money in separate bank accounts?
qa.right: It keeps reconciliation and reporting simple
wrong: It is required to use Open Banking
It removes the need for receipts
qa.why: Mixing makes it hard to see what is business spending.

qa.q: What does a password manager do?
qa.right: Stores and fills a unique password for each account
wrong: Chooses one password for all sites
Removes the need for a second sign-in step
Keeps passwords in a shared note
qa.why: Unique passwords limit the damage if one leaks.

qa.q: What is the difference between profit and cash flow?
qa.right: Profit is income less costs; cash flow is money actually moving in and out
wrong: Profit is cash in the bank
Cash flow is only for large firms
qa.why: A profitable business can still run short of cash.

qa.q: A caller says you must move money to a safe account at once. What is the best response?
qa.right: Hang up and call your bank on a number you already trust
wrong: Give the caller your card details to verify
Ask the caller for their number and call it
qa.why: Banks never ask you to move money to a safe account; urgency is a scam signal.

qa.q: A finalised VAT return is ready. What is true about submitting it in GGMoney?
qa.right: Submitting is a separate act with its own declaration
qa.why: HMRC has no way to withdraw a return, so submitting is a deliberate step.

qa.q: Why does a sync not change a reconciled transaction?
qa.right: It may sit inside a filed VAT return
wrong: The first sync always overrides them
qa.why: Reconciled rows are protected from later syncs.

qa.q: A transaction arrives by both feed and CSV import. What does GGMoney do?
qa.right: Recognises it as one transaction
qa.why: Both routes write to the same place and duplicates are recognised.

qa.q: How does GGMoney correct a mistake in a posted journal?
qa.right: By posting a reversal
wrong: By waiting for the next sync
qa.why: Posted journals are never edited, so both the error and the fix stay visible.

qa.q: Who must approve a filing in GGMoney?
qa.right: A second person; the app refuses self-approval
wrong: Only the person who prepared it
No one, because checks are automatic
qa.why: Filings need a second person, routine tasks one.

qa.q: An automatic check on a filing finds nothing wrong. What happens next?
qa.right: A person still has to sign it off
wrong: The check signs off for the second person
qa.why: Automatic checks report first but never sign anything off.

qa.q: Why does GGMoney store money as whole pence?
qa.right: To avoid rounding drift from decimal fractions
qa.why: Integers keep totals exact.

qa.q: A supplier emails to say its bank details have changed. What should you do before paying?
qa.right: Confirm using contact details you already trust
wrong: Reply to the email to confirm
Pay half to the new account to test
qa.why: Calling back on a known number defeats mandate fraud.

qa.q: What does the four-eyes principle mean?
qa.right: A second person checks important actions
qa.why: A second pair of eyes catches mistakes and fraud.

qa.q: Which statement about payroll rounding in GGMoney is correct?
qa.right: Rounding differs by tax on purpose
wrong: One rule is used for every figure
Pence are dropped from every deduction
qa.why: PAYE rounds down to the penny, NI to nearest, student loan down to whole pounds.

qa.q: Why do transactions before an account's opening date not appear?
qa.right: They are skipped
qa.why: Anything dated before the account opening date is skipped.

qa.q: A customer pays one amount that covers three invoices. Which feature records this?
qa.right: A payment allocation
qa.why: Payment allocations match one payment to several invoices.

qa.q: What does a trial balance check?
qa.right: That total debits equal total credits
qa.why: It lists every account balance so debits and credits can be compared.

qa.q: Which is a sign of an account takeover?
qa.right: Activity you did not carry out
qa.why: Stolen login details let someone act as you.

qa.q: What should you do first if you think you have paid a scammer?
qa.right: Tell your bank immediately
wrong: Wait to see if the money returns
qa.why: Quick contact with your bank gives the best chance of recovering funds.

qa.q: A feed has been working but transactions stop appearing after three months. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: The bank consent expired and needs renewing
wrong: The password was changed in GGMoney
qa.why: Open Banking consent lasts at most 90 days.

qa.q: You import a statement file that overlaps with the period the feed already covers. What should you expect?
qa.right: Overlapping transactions are recognised as the same
qa.why: Duplicates across routes are recognised as one.

qa.q: Which is NOT true of a finalised VAT return in GGMoney?
qa.right: It has already been sent to HMRC
wrong: It is a step before submission
qa.why: Finalising freezes figures; submitting is a separate act.

qa.q: Payroll will not file for a new tax year. What is the likely reason?
qa.right: The year's rates have not been verified
qa.why: A year is fileable only once its rates are verified.

qa.q: A message appears to come from your director asking for an urgent transfer. What is the best first step?
qa.right: Check by phone on a known number
wrong: Reply to the message for details
Forward it to a colleague to pay
qa.why: Urgency plus authority is the pattern of chief executive fraud.

qa.q: A buyer overpays and asks you to refund the difference. What is the safest response?
qa.right: Wait until the original payment has fully cleared and been verified
wrong: Ask the buyer to send a screenshot
qa.why: Overpayment scams rely on the original payment being reversed later.

qa.q: Why is a screenshot sent to support safer when passwords are hidden?
qa.right: Support does not need secrets to diagnose a problem
wrong: It stops the screenshot being copied
It is required by the bank
qa.why: Never expose passwords, codes or account numbers.

qa.q: A sync took in the last week of transactions only. Which sync was it?
qa.right: A later sync
qa.why: The first sync takes everything the bank allows; later syncs re-read the last week.

qa.q: Which is the most reliable way to avoid being caught by an urgent payment demand?
qa.right: Verify the request using a channel you already trust
wrong: Trust the logo in the message
qa.why: Verification through a separate trusted channel breaks the scam.

qa.q: Why is it risky to approve your own work in a finance tool?
qa.right: It removes the independent check
qa.why: Self-approval is refused for filings in GGMoney.

qa.q: A routine compliance task needs how many approvals in GGMoney?
qa.right: One person
qa.why: Filings need a second person; routine tasks need one.

qa.q: Why is rounding handled differently for different taxes?
qa.right: Using one rule for all would put a penny out on some payslips
qa.why: Each tax has its own rule on purpose.

qa.q: What is the main risk of a business email compromise?
qa.right: A real email account is used to redirect payments
qa.why: The request looks genuine because it comes from a real account.

qa.q: A payment arrives for the wrong amount from a customer and also lists an unknown reference. What should you do first?
qa.right: Investigate and match it to the correct invoice before recording
qa.why: Unexplained items should be queried before they are categorised.

qa.q: You share an unexpected recovery code with a caller who says it is for support. What does this expose?
qa.right: Your account to takeover
qa.why: Recovery codes should stay private; genuine support never needs them.

qa.q: A sandbox install shows a VAT return as submitted. What does that mean?
qa.right: Nothing was filed for real
qa.why: Sandbox mode runs against test services.

qa.q: A statement shows a balance that does not match the books and the difference is small. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Find and explain the difference before adjusting anything
qa.why: Small differences can hide errors or fraud.
